title: Reflex conditioning training- evaluation and implementation of a rehabilitation measure for patients with spastic hemiparesis of the lower extremity
summary:
The planned study looks at helping people who have a tight and weak leg after a stroke. The goal is to improve and test a type of training that can reduce certain unwanted muscle reactions in the lower leg. This should help to lessen the tightness and help the brain learn to control the leg better again.

The study wants to answer these questions: 

1. How well can this special training improve movement control in people who have a tight leg after a stroke

2. If the training is done only on the healthy leg, will the positive effect also transfer to the affected leg.

3. Are there long-term benefits of this training for the patients. And what factors decide whether someone responds well to this training or not?
conditions: Stroke, not specified as haemorrhage or infarction

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- 6-12 months post-stroke, after reaching a relatively stable plateau 
- unilateral plantar flexor spasticity (hemiparesis) 
- clearly recognizable stretch reflex upon mechanical stimulation of the pedal - no change in medication during the training intervention 
- ability to walk at least 10 m with or without assistance
Exclusion criteria:
- Motor neuron injury 
- history of myocardial infarction or heart failure 
- use of pacemakers or other active implants 
- a medically unstable condition 
- cognitive impairments that affect the ability to give informed consent or to successfully complete the protocol
